next_bounded_action.question: Does one fixed causal smoothing baseline reduce dynamic overestimation without losing genuine update accuracy?
next_bounded_action.source: existing policy10cal point predictions only; no model/raw features
next_bounded_action.method: EMA of predicted absolute EOL, alpha=2/(20+1) fixed from existing20cycle memory; initialize at origin100 same model EOL; Ehat_t=(1-alpha)*Ehat_previous+alpha*(t+saved_RUL_t); predicted RUL=max(0,Ehat_t-t). No true residual or future information used by recurrence.
next_bounded_action.validation: same10cells4567origins; existing >=5pct TimeMAE gain,>=7/10cells,bootstrap2000seed42CIlo>0,over100increment<=.01; compare vs unsmoothedpolicy, report expired count/update lag/harmful revisions. IfFAIL stop this fixedbaseline, no alpha/window/seed rescue.
next_bounded_action.scope: strong simple point update baseline, not innovation or calibrated probability distribution; all earlier probability NO_GO retained
